big_case_rationale: Resolves a four-circuit split on how race-neutral proxies in selective K-12 admissions are tested after SFFA; affects many large districts' admissions policies.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority holds that under Arlington Heights a plaintiff challenging a facially neutral admissions policy need not show that the targeted racial group's overall admission share fell below its share of the applicant pool; because the Equal Protection Clause protects individuals, it suffices that the policy was adopted at least in part because of its adverse effect on members of the group (e.g., a before-and-after decline or burden on individual applicants), rejecting the Fourth Circuit's Coalition for TJ aggregate benchmark.

The holding is narrow in reach: the Court rejects only the aggregate-underrepresentation threshold as a categorical precondition and expressly declines to decide whether this complaint plausibly alleges discriminatory intent, remanding that question to the Fourth Circuit, and does not hold that race-neutral proxies adopted to change racial composition are per se subject to strict scrutiny.
